newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady-up, pork bellies steady-off.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady-up, pork bellies steady-off.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called steady to 0.200 lower, analysts said.

Steady to higher cash hog indications on reduced hog runs was expected to provide early support in hog futures. Although cash pork product values fell Tuesday, packers need hogs and are willing to raise bids to compete for the lighter than expected supply, analysts said.
One analyst noted that cash loin prices held steady and this sometimes has more influence on packer demand then other cuts which were mostly lower.
The latest CME lean hog index was up $0.11 to $80.88 per cwt.

Although pork bellies showed some technical support after bouncing from lows Tuesday and the out-of-town report showed a net out-movement despite larger hog kills, the futures market is expected to be under pressure. Cash belly prices fell sharply on Tuesday to lowest levels since early May and will likely weigh on sentiment, they said.
Cash bellies fell $3 to $7 per cwt with 14-16 lb bellies ranging down to $75.
